title: a nested call that cannot be resolved is reported under the name of the function that could
label: REPRODUCED-TODAY

measurement.why: the same defect reported two ways on one node: bare it says 'unknown signature: convert_from(string, string)'; nested inside split_part it says 'split_part(): unknown signature: convert_from(string, string) (returning <string>)'

nested_two_deep.message: upper(): split_part(): unknown signature: convert_from(string, string) (returning <string>)

claim_A_explicit_string_cast_required.note: does not hold: convert_from applied to a bytes column resolves inside split_part with no cast at all, and reports its return type as 'text'

claim_B_local_versus_cloud_divergence.note: does not hold as a platform difference: on this one node, the statement fails on a text column and resolves on a bytes column. The variable that changed between our two runs was the column type, which our own comment records (demo_world.sql:848-850, 'a scratch table written from memory made the same mistake').
claim_B_local_versus_cloud_divergence.why_not_re_run: running this statement on CockroachDB Cloud means driving DDL or seeds at a shared live cluster, which the critique plan forbids (R4)

transcript.what: create a table shaped like the one the original statement ran against
transcript.sql: CREATE TABLE checkpoint (id INT8 PRIMARY KEY, body STRING NOT NULL, root_hash BYTES NOT NULL)

transcript.what: put one row in it, with a three-line note in body
transcript.sql: INSERT INTO checkpoint VALUES (1, 'mainline/site' || chr(10) || '2' || chr(10) || 'deadbeef' || chr(10), b'\x01\x02')

transcript.what: read the column types from the catalogue rather than assuming them
transcript.sql: SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'checkpoint' ORDER BY column_name
transcript.note: body is text and root_hash is bytea; the original comment says this was checked rather than assumed, and this is that check

transcript.what: ask the database which argument types convert_from actually accepts
transcript.sql: SELECT p.proname || '(' || pg_catalog.pg_get_function_arguments(p.oid) || ')' FROM pg_proc p WHERE p.proname = 'convert_from'
transcript.note: one overload only: it takes raw bytes, so handing it text is our error and the database is right to refuse

transcript.what: THE MISTAKE, BARE: hand a text column to convert_from
transcript.note: clear and correct: it names convert_from, which is the call that is wrong

transcript.what: THE FINDING: the identical mistake with split_part wrapped around it
transcript.note: same defect, same SQLSTATE, but the message now opens with the name of the function that resolved fine

transcript.what: and one level deeper again, to see whether the outer names accumulate
transcript.error: 42883 upper(): split_part(): unknown signature: convert_from(string, string) (returning <string>)

transcript.what: a different outer function, to show the prefix is the caller and not split_part in particular
a different inner function, to show this is not about convert_from in particular
the repair: give convert_from the bytes it asked for
what the product ships instead: no convert_from at all, because body is already text
claim A: does convert_from's result need an explicit ::STRING before split_part accepts it?
transcript.note: no cast anywhere in this statement; if it resolves, claim A does not hold

transcript.what: claim A, asked directly: what type does convert_from say it returns?
